source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
SJC11 publishes 73,000 square feet of technical space and no IT load figure in megawatts. Because no power figure is published, no rack or accelerator estimate is possible here. The 73,000 square feet of raised-floor or white-space area is a meaningful signal of physical scale, but floor area alone does not determine AI hosting capacity, because power density per square foot varies widely across facility designs and tenants.

The certifications qualify the campus to host regulated workloads. SOC 2 Type 2 and SSAE 18 attest to audited operational controls. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment-card data environments. HIPAA qualifies it for protected health information. LEED and Green Globes are environmental design and operations ratings, not security or reliability attestations. None of these certifications speak to power density or the facility's suitability for GPU-scale AI training, which is not a compliance category.

California has 103 mapped data center facilities in this site's dataset, of which only 5 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 170 MW across those five. SJC11 ranks sixth by published megawatts, which in practice means it falls outside the five facilities that publish any power figure at all, so it cannot be ranked on power. Within the Santa Clara County concentration of compute infrastructure, SJC11 is a mid-scale colocation facility whose relevance to AI workloads depends on power specifications the operator has not published.
